name: ucon64
desc: ROM backup tool and emulator's Swiss Army knife program
why: A ROM format swiss army knife that identifies and rewrites console dumps, a fun look into old cartridge file formats, though niche.

brief.what_it_is: uCON64 is a command-line tool for backing up, identifying, patching and managing video game ROM and SRAM files. It reads ROM dumps for many consoles, handhelds and arcade systems and prints verbose information about each one. It can also rewrite and modify ROMs, and it can create and check RomCenter DAT files to detect bad dumps. Its homepage also lists support for backup hardware that copies ROMs and SRAM to and from real carts, and for patch formats (IPS, APS, BSL, PPF, Game Genie). Input is ROM or SRAM files, and output is identified, converted, patched or copied files. The homepage does not say what the output looks like beyond the verbose information it prints.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as "the backup tool and wonderful emulator's Swiss Army knife program". It is aimed at people who dump, back up and manage cartridge and console data for emulators and hardware, and it is distributed under the GNU GPL.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not describe internals. It says ROM format support is "continuously added and updated" and that DAT files are used "for secure detection of bad dumps". Commands take a ROM file and options such as --mkdat=DATFILE, which generates a DAT file from ROMs.

commands_seen.context: Option named on the DAT files section of the homepage; it generates DAT files for all known ROMs (written as 'uCON64 option: --mkdat=DATFILE'). This is an option string, not a full command line.
Named as a uCON64 option in the loader descriptions for Flash Advance Linker, MD-PRO, SMS-PRO, GG-PRO, PCE-PRO and Super Flash. Option string only, not a full command line.
Named alongside --multi as an option for the Flash Advance Linker loader (preboot32.zip). Option string only.
Named alongside --multi as an option for the MD-PRO loader (mdpacku4.zip). Option string only.
Named as the uCON64 option for the Lynxit custom Atari Lynx backup unit (lynxit11.zip). Option string only.
Named as the uCON64 option for the NES emulator for GameBoy by Kami (fcgb2.lzh). Option string only.
Named as the uCON64 option for the Ultra SMS Sega Master System/Game Gear emulator for Nintendo 64 (ultrasmsv10.zip). Option string only.

brief.install_notes: The brew caveats say to copy or move DAT files into $HOME/.ucon64/dat and to check $HOME/.ucon64rc for configuration after the first run. The homepage lists source tarballs and zips, a Linux x86_64 binary tarball, Windows binaries built with MinGW, Visual C++ and Cygwin, and a DOS binary. It also names FreeBSD Ports, OpenBSD packages and pkgsrc as install routes. Some backup units need extra files: USB support is a separate Windows build for Quickdev16 and Super UFO Pro 8 SD. Parallel-port access on Windows needs an I/O port driver such as giveio, giveio64, DlPortIO or ioport. DOS needs csdpmi5b.zip. Loader and support files are separate downloads from the homepage.
brief.standout: Hardware support is the unusual part: the homepage lists loaders and support files for many cartridge backup units, flash carts and N64 and GB devices, alongside ROM identification and patching. Few other ROM tools cover the physical copier side too.
brief.status: Apparently quiet. The homepage's newest news item is dated 20211122 (uCON64 2.2.2 released), and the downloads are still 2.2.2. The homepage shows no later news and did not show a last commit date. I did not check the SVN or any repository, so this is based on the homepage alone.
brief.caveats: The homepage is old-looking and some links were not checked. Support for backup units depends on manufacturers cooperating, and the homepage says so. Many backup-unit features need Windows drivers, DOS extenders or separate loader zips. The homepage lists the DAT files as 'completely new, tested and working' but only offers a handful of them, with the note 'to be continued...'. I did not find a Homebrew-specific install page; the brew caveats are the only Homebrew guidance I saw. The brew description and scout notes are the source for the 'niche' label, and the homepage does not contradict it.
quotes: uCON64 is the backup tool and wonderful emulator's Swiss Army knife program
uCON64 is completely Open Source Software and has been ported to many platforms using code from various people
Support for almost every video game system (Consoles, Handheld, and Arcade) with very verbose ROM information is continuously added and updated

fetch_log: https://ucon64.sourceforge.io/ — worked; returned the homepage text with news, feature list, download links, hardware support and loader notes. No separate README, install page or FAQ was fetched; I stopped after one fetch because the homepage had enough for the brief.
